column1: # Recoil pattern SHAPE - the authored (judgement) input of gen_recoil_pattern.py. The physics (cartridge, weight, rate) is
# NOT here: it comes from recoil_research.tsv (published specs, per-gun sources) overridden by recoil_measured.tsv wherever a
# MEASURED figure exists. This file only says how each game weapon maps onto that physics and how the kick is SHAPED.
# stem     game tik stem (models/weapons/<stem>.tik). Finish variants (<stem>_<finish>) need no row: the engine drops trailing
#          _segments until a row matches, so they share their base gun's pattern. A MODEL variant that is a different real gun
#          (thompsonsmg_tommy28 = an M1928) gets its own row here and matches first.
# phys     key of the physics row in recoil_research.tsv
# cls      A automatic (SMG / AR / LMG / MG)  S semi-auto rifle  B bolt / pump / break  P pistol / revolver  L launcher
# extra_kg mass added to (or taken from) the spec weight: a scope ~0.4, a suppressor ~0.3, a lighter model variant < 0
# mag_kg   loaded magazine / drum / belt carried on the gun (the spec weights are EMPTY); estimates, from the cartridge count
# layout   stock line: drop (the bore well above the shoulder - climbs), inline (straight-line stock - pushes back), mid,
#          thompson (the dropped stock Aberdeen 1942 measured: an in-line stock raised hits 61->81 pct at 50 yd), pistol
# device   none, cutts, brake, jacket (PPSh slanted jacket compensator), suppressor, booster (MG42 muzzle recoil booster)
# hip      hip-fire (no sights) multiplier on the kick
# drift    horizontal drift per round as a share of the climb, + = right (right-handed shooter)
# sway     horizontal sway amplitude, share of the climb;  period  rounds per sway cycle
# jitP     random vertical share (+-);  jitY  random horizontal share (+-)
# scale    final trim (1 = the physics as derived) - every value off 1 says why in basis
# basis    where the SHAPE comes from: [M] measured / documented, [D] derived from layout or physics, [A] anecdotal

column15: [M] Aberdeen 1942: climb from the dropped stock (in-line stock 61->81 pct hits at 50 yd). [A] climbs up and right for a right-handed shooter
[M] as thompsonsmg; the 50 rd drum adds ~2.2 kg forward (heavier, slower to climb)
[M] M1928A1 with Cutts (Aberdeen: the Cutts gave no net gain in hits - smoke on the sights - so it only trims the climb a little). [A] up-right
[M] slow measured rate (400-550) chosen for burst control; [D] mild, nearly vertical
[D] mp40 + suppressor mass and gas trap
[D] MP18: wooden dropped stock, side magazine. [M] MP28 burst groups moved right (Soviet 1941 trial)
[M] Soviet Dec 1941 trial: MP28 burst groups shift right (+4.8 horizontal vs +1.8 vertical over single shots)
[D] light skeleton gun, side magazine: a vertical bounce rather than a steady walk; [M] 1941 trial found it accurate
[M] Soviet Dec 1941 trial: burst groups spread mostly SIDEWAYS (+7.8 horizontal, +1.3 vertical vs single shots), 1050 rpm measured; the jacket compensator holds the muzzle down
[D] PPS-43 at a lower rate (630 measured), folding stock; drift as the PPSh, smaller
[D] 450 rpm, heavy bolt: the slowest, most controllable .45 - nearly straight up
[D] MAB 38A: heavy wooden stock and a ported compensator
[D] 8 mm Nambu is a weak round; the 1944 model's 800 rpm builds it
[D] heavy and muzzle-heavy: a big but steady, nearly vertical climb
[D] M1918 (7.25 kg, no bipod) - lighter, climbs more
[D] Lewis gun: 13 kg with the 47 rd pan - heavy, steady
[M] US ETO Ordnance Oct 1944: marked climb, 5 rd bursts not held on a 6x6 ft target at 35 yd - scale 1.15 for that report
[M] 2nd pattern, straight-line stock and muzzle brake; McCollum: little visible climb in SHORT bursts, long bursts walk off - the light gun's hard kick per round with a pattern that tapers early
[D] Vickers-Berthier: 11.1 kg, slow rate - very stable
[M] hands-on: a rocking front-to-back recoil from the heavy bolt, manageable held tight - a small bounce, almost no walk; scale 0.9 for its reputation as the steadiest LMG
[D] M1919A6 14.7 kg - held off the bipod it is a heavy, slow-rising gun

[M] Soviet manual for captured guns: from the bipod the cone leaves the target after 7 rounds (bursts of 5-7); 1100-1350 rpm measured. [D] off the mount the booster and the rate make it violent - mounting cuts it (coop_braceKickMG)
[D] one big shove, straight back and up; follow-ups climb if rushed
[D] 5.4 J free recoil in a 2.4 kg rifle - light, quick to come back
[D] recoil-operated .30-06; the moving barrel softens the peak a little
[D] SVT-40 muzzle brake takes the edge off a stout cartridge
[D] the hardest-kicking standard rifle here: heavy bullet, light rifle
[D] .303 in a 4.1 kg rifle - softer than the Mauser
[D] 6.5 mm - the mildest service bolt rifle here
[D] subsonic .45 in an integrally suppressed carbine - very little kick
[D] 12 ga full load in a 3.6 kg gun: the biggest shoulder shove of the long guns
[D] lighter double: snaps up harder than the pump
[D] .45 ACP, high bore axis: a sharp flip that comes straight back
[D] the downed sidearm fires as the Colt
[D] steep grip, low bore axis toggle: a softer flip than the P38
[D] weak 8 mm in a heavy frame
[D] slow heavy .455: a big roll up
[D] integrally suppressed, manual bolt - almost no flip
[D] broomhandle: high bore line, light round
[D] with the shoulder stock fitted it handles as a light carbine
[D] recoilless: the rocket burns out in the tube, a small shove
[M] the one launcher that kicks: its spigot spring recoil is documented as powerful
